changes.final: drawn vertical strokes with asymmetric hooked feet
changes.shows: The left shaft ends in a small rounded left hook; the right ends in a much smaller leftward foot. Neither has an ordinary two-sided arrowhead. Both shapes are reproduced without adding an edge label.
The right leg is an open curve detached just below the top bar, and a separate handwritten p is clearly below the symbol.
The G has no independent horizontal rule beneath it; the following m sits below and to the right.
Two nested contours and an inner upright favour a double impression, but do not securely distinguish the alphabet from accidental overtyping.
The legs are nearly straight with a small left foot and a slight curve on the right. The hand does not securely distinguish lowercase π from capital Π here.
Both product signs have the typewriter x serifs.
The square right coefficient and first-sequence coefficient have one oval body, a tail and an independent underline.
The first crossed cell retains a comma tail, then a crossed blank cell, then visible u and n bodies.
There is one clear g cell, followed by a cell containing a second g lower loop and an r-like shoulder, then amme. The image does not support inserting an additional separate g cell.
The same cell has u uprights and a dark y descender. Both layers are visible, but their order is uncertain.
A rising curved stroke runs from before près toward the added can.

changes.C: rules under Proposition, monomorphisme, Question; numbers outside
changes.shows: The rules stop beneath the words, leaving the handwritten numbers beyond them.
The opening and closing marks are doubled upright strokes at the top of the word.
The line break falls after partic uli without a visible hyphen; the next line begins e followed by a cell with a tall t stem/foot and an r shoulder. The t is the darker dominant shape.
The o and n bodies, a bowl, and u-n-e remain readable through the x row, including crossed spaces.
The capital G bottom is appreciably above the baseline of alois; it is reproduced raised without inferring an exponent.

The pale lower trace has a long left stroke and a curved central/right body. Mu is favoured, but pi and an earlier erased state remain possible; no separate cancelling line crosses the surviving lower strokes.
A dark blue/black cancellation covers a raised mark beside the G; the old glyph cannot be securely recovered.

The outer curve suggests 6, but dark crossing strokes obscure its lower loop. The question number is not used to resolve it.
